verdict: Meta's revenue rose 26% to $51.2B on strong ads — but a one-time $15.9B tax charge from the new U.S. tax law cut reported profit to $2.7B; without it, profit was $18.6B.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger: impressions grew 14% and the average price per ad rose 10%.

segments.name: Family of Apps other revenue
segments.note: WhatsApp business messaging, Meta Verified subscriptions and other app income; up 59% YoY.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.note: Quest headsets and AI glasses; sales rose 74% and the unit lost $4.4B at the operating level.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI research (Meta Superintelligence Labs), engineers and Reality Labs development; up 35% YoY.

opex.name: Marketing & sales
opex.note: Selling ads and marketing Meta's apps and devices.

otherDetail: Meta reports one combined line, interest and other income (expense), net; this quarter it was a $1,128M net gain.
follow100Note: The tax slice is swollen by a one-time, non-cash $15.9B tax charge from the new U.S. tax law. Without it, tax would have taken about $5.90 of each $100 and Meta would have kept about $36.37 as profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Ads kept growing fast
takeaways.text: Advertising revenue rose 26% to $50.1B: ad impressions grew 14% and the average price per ad rose 10%. The Family of Apps earned $25.0B of operating profit.

takeaways.title: A one-time tax charge crushed reported profit
takeaways.text: A non-cash tax charge from the new U.S. tax law (remeasuring deferred tax assets under the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax) pushed Meta's tax rate to 87%. Reported net income was $2.7B; excluding the charge it was $18.6B, and EPS was $7.25 rather than $1.05.

takeaways.title: The AI bill keeps climbing
takeaways.text: Capital spending was $19.4B in the quarter, including finance leases, and free cash flow was $10.6B. For 2025 Meta raised its capex plan to $70-72B.

oneTimers: A one-time, non-cash income tax charge of $15.93B — from remeasuring deferred tax assets after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act changed how the U.S. Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax applies — pushed Meta's effective tax rate to 87% and cut net income to $2.71B (EPS $1.05). Excluding the charge, net income was $18.64B (EPS $7.25) and the tax rate was 14%. Meta expects the law to significantly reduce its U.S. federal cash tax payments for the remainder of 2025 and in future years.
